rationale: C15 plausibly supplied concrete drafting machinery for the child's treatment of civilian reservists. Most distinctively, both directives restrict outside personnel to advisory or otherwise limited functions and then exempt them from the identical enumerated conflict-of-interest statutes. The child's section 5 compresses and adapts C15's detailed appointment regime to training-only Executive Reservists. C11 contains substantially the same older machinery and is therefore a strong alternative, while C19 combines a defense-mobilization body of outside members with the same statutory exemptions but is less closely aligned with the child's restrictions on their activities.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Activities of persons by reason of designation as Executive Reservists under this order shall not include acting or advising on any matter pending before any department or agency but shall be limited to receiving training for mobilization assignments under the Reserve program.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: All persons appointed pursuant to the authority delegated by subsection 101 (a) of this order ... shall, when policy matters are involved, be limited to advising appropriate, full-time Government officials who are responsible for making policy decisions.
shared_material.explanation: Both establish explicit boundaries on what participating private-sector personnel may do for the Government; the child adapts C15's advisory-role limitation into a stricter training-only limitation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: reservists who are not full-time Government employees shall be exempt from the operation of sections 281, 283, 284, 434, and 1914 of Title 18, United States Code, and section 190 of the Revised Statutes (5 U.S.C. 99).
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Any person employed pursuant to the authority delegated by subsection 101 (a) of this order is exempted, with respect to such employment, by section 710 (b) (4) of the Act from the operation of sections 281, 283, 284, 434, and 1914 of title 18 of the United States Code, and section 190 of the Revised Statutes (5 U.S.C. 99)
shared_material.explanation: This is a distinctive, nearly verbatim reproduction of the same six-part statutory exemption, applied to a new class of defense-mobilization personnel.
